sentences.text: Eocypselus is a basal form of the order Apodiformes, a group that includes modern hummingbirds, tree swifts, and swifts.
The species E. rowei was less than 5 inches from head to tail, yet feathers made up more than half of its wingspan.
The type species Eocypselus vincenti was named by C.J.O. Harrison in 1984 based on fossils from the London Clay Formation of England.
A second species, Eocypselus rowei, was described in 2013 by Ksepka and colleagues in honor of John Rowe, whom they considered a "fossil geek."
Mayr and Kitchener described three additional Eocypselus species in 2024.
Ksepka stated that Eocypselus represents the closest known relative to the point where swifts and hummingbirds diverged.
Eocypselus lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
